scope: D0 workspace-write revocation ordering and D1 Team PR comparison gaps

checks.name: Fresh PostgreSQL 17 replay
checks.detail: 41 ordered migrations applied to a fresh database with Auth, Realtime publication and Cron stand-ins; unavailable pg_cron extension creation omitted

checks.name: SQL access and write tests
checks.detail: Five suites and 34 pgTAP-equivalent assertions passed, including four new task write/revocation assertions

checks.name: Two-session write/revocation race
checks.detail: A writer was observed sleeping inside an open transaction after its guarded insert; membership deletion waited 3.94 seconds for commit; a subsequent write returned WORKSPACE_WRITE_DENIED. This used the disposable PostgreSQL stand-in, not hosted Supabase.

checks.name: React, Orders and Billing verified change
checks.detail: known-bad failures and repaired passes reproduced in separate checkouts; prior proof became stale; repaired coverage remains unknown

observations: The workspace-scoped write trigger now locks the workspace, workspace membership and organization membership rows while authorizing task, context, evidence, comment, receipt, graph and PR row writes.
A queued row write is denied after workspace or organization membership removal; a write that obtains the shared lock first serializes ahead of the revocation transaction.
The repository-binding broker now receives explicit service-role project table privileges, which a minimal fresh deployment needs for its locked upsert.
Team PR assessment maps the old path of a rename and a deletion, while renamed, deleted, generated and uninspectable paths keep the assessment incomplete.

Selected OpenAPI 3 JSON comparison now surfaces changed request schema constraints, path-level parameter schemas, and response fields that cease to be required. Unresolved response or parameter references keep the comparison partial.
limits: The PostgreSQL replay used stand-ins and did not exercise real Supabase JWT issuance, PostgREST, Storage or Realtime with two identities.
The two-session race test proves PostgreSQL row-lock ordering in the disposable stand-in, but has not been repeated through hosted Supabase PostgREST or background jobs.
Task, evidence, PR, snapshot and change-feed payloads still require a complete repository-rights audit and brokered or redacted projections.
OpenAPI comparison covers selected JSON structure; YAML, broader schema semantics and independent consumer discovery remain incomplete.
Team has no accepted common exact-target execution receipt and cannot show a verified pass. The local repaired fixture remains unknown for relevance and discovery.
D0 and D1 completion gates remain open.
